title: The evolution of ornithischian nomenclature
content:
Abstract
Comprising two of the three taxa originally referred to Dinosauria, the members of Ornithischia have played a key role in the historical development of dinosaur taxonomy and nomenclature. Over refinements in the understanding of ornithischian evolution, 257 different taxon names for ornithischian groups have been published, with only 96 being available as established clade names with formalized phylogenetic definitions. Many of these historic names can be considered approximate synonyms of names in current use, but it is important that the original applications of these names are identified, proper attribution is established, and their later uses detailed, to fulfil the recommendations of the International Code of Phylogenetic Nomenclature (PhyloCode) and allow for consistent communication. Evaluating the synonymy of taxon names shows that 126 unique ornithischian clade names can be identified based on current phylogenetic reconstructions, 31 of which have not been formally defined. The difficulty in recognizing whether certain nomenclatural concepts are the same arises from two primary factors: poorly-known nominal taxa and insufficiently supported hypotheses of phylogenetic relationships. The recognition of these shortcomings allows guidance for future application of taxon names that can lead to consistent use, minimal disruptions as relationships change with further study, and a clearer ability to communicate taxonomic content.
